name: The five bills a Chinese tender is made of
name_zh: 工程量清单的五部分构成
review_status: Derived from GB 50500-2013 read in full for the structures it states. Pending review by a Chinese cost engineer (造价工程师) for current practice.
references: GB 50500-2013 建设工程工程量清单计价规范
description: A Chinese tender price is not one list with a margin on the end. It is five bills that are summed in a fixed order, and two of the five are priced by rules rather than by competition. Importing a Chinese bill as a single flat list of measured works loses roughly the whole of the preliminaries and the whole of the statutory content, which on a building job is not a rounding difference.

bills.name: measured works
bills.note: the items with twelve-digit codes, priced at comprehensive unit rates

bills.name: measure items
bills.note: splits in two. 单价措施项目 are measured and priced at a rate (scaffolding, formwork, vertical transport). 总价措施项目 are lump sums taken as a percentage (safe and civilised construction, night work, secondary handling, completion clean).

components.name: provisional sum, held by the employer and spent only on instruction
prime cost sums, for materials (材料暂估价) and for nominated specialist works (专业工程暂估价)
main contractor attendance on employer-appointed specialists and on employer-supplied materials

practice_notes: The order is fixed and the tax sits last, on top of everything else including the statutory charges
暂列金额 belongs to the employer for the whole of the job. It is in the contract sum and is not the contractor's money until an instruction spends it
A bill that shows only bill 1 is a measured-works schedule, not a tender price
